title: e2e: create a submission, get generated questions, edit them, and see edits survive reload
description:
The core journey: /submissions/new, pick student, enter title + text, submit, land on the detail page, see the stubbed question set appear, then edit a question, add a manual question, reorder (Move question <n> up/down) and remove one (Remove question <n> from the set). Reload and confirm every change persisted.

Catches regressions page tests can't: generation kicked off from the real server function (viva-voce-ai-zaq), reload mid-generation (viva-voce-ai-xvx), RLS on viva_questions writes, ordering persisted in the DB.
acceptance_criteria:
- Spec runs against the AI stub and asserts the fixture question texts
- After reload the edited/added/reordered/removed state matches what the teacher did
- Rows are tagged and cleaned up by the data-isolation hook

title: Stub the OpenAI boundary so e2e runs offline and deterministically
description:
The running app calls OpenAI from the server and the browser:
- generateSubmissionViva.ts and assessmentSummaryOpenAi.ts: @ai-sdk/openai default provider
- vivaTranscription.ts: hardcoded https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions
- realtimeTokenServerFn.ts: hardcoded .../v1/realtime/client_secrets
- useLiveTranscription.ts: wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime from the browser

Real calls cost money, need network, and return different questions on every run, so assertions can't be stable. Make the base URL configurable (one OPENAI_BASE_URL read in one place, createOpenAI({ baseURL }) for the SDK calls), then have the e2e package start a small stub server that returns fixture responses. Reuse the fixtures in apps/web/src/test/handlers.ts + factories.ts where possible (msw/node setupServer behind a tiny HTTP server, or a plain node:http stub). The browser realtime socket can be intercepted with e2e's browser API mocking (docs: Working with the browser) or left out of e2e scope; decide and note it.

Default to the stub in e2e. Allow an opt-in real-OpenAI run (env flag) for a manual or nightly smoke.
acceptance_criteria:
- With OPENAI_API_KEY unset or fake, an e2e run makes no request to api.openai.com (checked by the stub logging unmatched routes or by network policy)
- Question generation returns a known fixture set the specs can assert on by text
- Production behaviour is unchanged when OPENAI_BASE_URL is unset (covered by existing unit tests)

title: Route transitions flash an unrelated page (detail, login, idle navigation)
description: Opening a submission flashes 'Preparing viva questions' while questions load; login shows the form under /submissions while the user is re-fetched; navigations after the 30s user cache expires can show the list-shaped AuthenticatedPending skeleton. Fix on branch fix/route-transition-flash.

title: byteRange test fails on main: stops reading the file once the range has been sent
description: apps/web/src/utils/byteRange.test.ts:148 expects onCancel to be called once after a range is served; it is called 0 times. Reproduces 3/3 on clean origin/main (b464a6a) with: cd apps/web && pnpm exec vitest run src/utils/byteRange.test.ts

title: Transcript disappears when you leave the submission page and return
description:
The transcript panel is empty after navigating to the submissions table and back, even though the recording is still there.

The segments are persisted correctly in viva_transcript_segments — nothing is lost. The page just never looks them up again. vivaSessionId (submissions.$submissionId.tsx:602) is component state whose only writer is resolveVivaSessionId, which runs when a recording STARTS. A remount resets it to null, so transcriptQuery's 'enabled: Boolean(vivaSessionId)' gate keeps the query from ever firing, assembleTranscript([]) returns '', and the panel shows its empty placeholder.

The audio player comes back fine because it is keyed on submissionId, so the teacher sees a recording with no transcript beside it. The same gap loses the transcript view on a page reload mid-viva.

The conduct page already does this correctly — it loads the session from the database on mount and derives everything from vivaSession?.id. The detail page has queries for the submission, its questions, and its audio, but none for its viva session.

A submission keeps one recording (replaceEarlierRecordings), and ended sessions accumulate while only one can be active per question set, so the transcript to show is the most recent session's.
acceptance_criteria: Leaving the submission page and returning still shows the stored transcript; a reload does too; starting a new recording still shows the live feed.
close_reason: Detail page now fetches the latest viva session on mount; transcript reads back.

title: Start viva generation on create instead of after navigation
description:
Generation currently queues behind three sequential waits: the Supabase insert in submissions.new.tsx, a hard route change, then submissionQuery+questionsQuery settling on the detail page. Only then does the effect at submissions.$submissionId.tsx:816 call runGeneration(). The LLM request has not started until the last of those completes.

Kick off generation as soon as the insert returns so the model call overlaps navigation and query settle. Cleanest shape is one server function that inserts the submission and starts generation.

This is pure latency the teacher feels as a dead wait.
acceptance_criteria: The generation request is in flight before the detail route finishes mounting; measured time from click to questions visible drops by the navigation+query settle time.
close_reason: Generation now starts on create; detail page claims the in-flight run from the registry.

title: Reloading during viva generation shows a false failure
description:
Reloading the submission page while viva question generation is still running shows 'We finished reading this submission but did not produce any viva questions.' even though generation is succeeding in the background.

The hasGenerationBeenAttempted sessionStorage guard (apps/web/src/routes/_authed/submissions.$submissionId.tsx:416) sets hasCompletedGeneration=true on remount. With questions.length still 0, the branch at line 910 renders SubmissionGenerationFailure. Its 'Try again' button then starts a duplicate generation run.

The guard conflates 'a run was started' with 'a run finished'. It needs real status (pending/running/completed/failed) persisted rather than an attempted boolean, so a reload resumes the waiting state.
acceptance_criteria: Reloading mid-generation keeps showing the waiting state and completes normally; no false failure copy; no duplicate generation run.
close_reason: Fixed: status record replaces the attempted flag; reload mid-run polls instead of reporting a false failure.

title: Live viva recording and chunk transcription
description: Wire the record CTA on the submission detail page to the existing chunked capture, and transcribe each chunk as it lands. Session is created only after mic permission is granted, so a declined prompt leaves no orphan session. Stop assembles the timeslices into one playable file on submission_viva. New viva_transcript_segments table holds text keyed by chunk sequence.

title: Wire the Record button on the submission page to real capture
description: The submission detail page now leads with a Record CTA, but it is inert. It must start a viva session (creating the question set row it needs), capture audio, and save it against the submission. Conduct mode (/submissions/:id/conduct) is currently unreachable from the UI because the readiness/session-start panel was removed - the Record flow replaces it.
close_reason: Record button now creates a session and drives the real capture pipeline.

title: Fix local Supabase db:start students relation collision
description: pnpm db:start fails during local Supabase startup because the first migration attempts to create public.students when it already exists. Diagnose the source and make local database startup repeatable.
close_reason: Local Supabase startup now succeeds after moving configured local ports from stale Docker-forwarded 543xx ports to 553xx; verified db:start and seeded students count.

title: Fix db:start command
description: Investigate why the db:start command is not working and make the minimal fix needed so the project database can be started reliably.

title: Trigger generation after submission creation
description:
Wire the create-submission UX into the AI generation workflow.

Why:
The current form creates a submission and returns to the submissions list. The next phase needs creation to kick off viva generation and keep the teacher informed while it runs.

Work:
- update the create flow so generation is triggered after the submission is saved
- choose a user flow that keeps the teacher oriented, likely redirecting to the submission detail page with a visible loading state
- preserve clear feedback for submission-create failures versus generation failures
- ensure the generated result appears without forcing a confusing manual refresh path

Acceptance criteria:
- creating a submission starts generation for that submission
- the user sees a clear loading state while waiting for the questions
- success and failure outcomes are routed into the submission detail experience cleanly

title: Add submission detail page with generated viva output
description:
Create a dedicated submission detail route at `/submissions/{id}`.

Why:
Teachers need a stable place to read the full submission alongside the generated viva questions and scoring output.

Work:
- add a route and data-loading path for a single submission by id
- render the submission title, student, full text, and creation metadata
- render generated viva output when available, including categories, teacher notes, score breakdown, strengths, and next steps
- render appropriate empty/loading/error states when generation has not finished or has failed

Acceptance criteria:
- a teacher can open `/submissions/{id}` and read the submission in full
- generated viva output is shown on the same page when available
- the page handles in-progress and failed generation states clearly

title: Generate viva analysis with AI SDK
description:
Implement the server-side generation pipeline for submission viva analysis.

Why:
After a submission is created, its text must be sent to an LLM using the provided KS4 prompt and returned in a structured format that can be stored safely.

Work:
- use the AI SDK for the generation call
- encode the provided prompt and output contract into a server-side interface
- validate and normalize model output before persistence
- persist generated questions, score data, and teacher guidance against the submission
- record generation failures without losing the underlying submission

Acceptance criteria:
- given a persisted submission, the app can request an AI viva analysis and save the result
- malformed or incomplete model output is handled explicitly rather than silently accepted
- failures are stored in a way the UI can surface and recover from later

title: Persist submission viva analyses and questions
description:
Add the database model for generated viva output attached to a submission.

Why:
The app currently stores submissions only. To support LLM-generated teacher questions and scoring, we need a stable persistence model keyed to a submission.

Work:
- decide the storage shape for a generated analysis, including foreign keys back to submissions
- store the 12 generated questions with category and teacher note data
- store the writing score, category breakdown, strengths, next steps, teacher guidance, and generation status/error metadata
- add the required migrations, indexes, and row-level security policies for authenticated reads/writes

Acceptance criteria:
- a submission can have generated viva data persisted and queried later
- the schema supports loading, success, and failure states for generation
- the persistence model is documented clearly enough for frontend and server work to build against it
close_reason: Closed

title: Generate AI viva analysis for submissions
description:
Build the next phase of the submissions feature so each submission can be analysed by an LLM, persisted, and reviewed by a teacher.

Scope:
- generate a structured viva output from a submission using the provided KS4 prompt
- persist generated questions, score breakdown, guidance, and generation state against a submission
- add a submission detail page that shows the full submission and generated output
- update the submission creation flow so generation is triggered after create and the UI reflects in-progress work

Success looks like:
- a teacher can open a submission and review generated viva questions and scoring guidance
- generation is tracked in the data model and UI with clear loading/error/success states
- the implementation is split into small tasks that can be worked asynchronously

title: Run the e2e suite on pull requests in GitHub Actions
description:
New workflow (or a job in deploy-cloudflare.yml) following https://e2e.tester.army/docs/ci/github-actions.md:
- setup-node from .nvmrc, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
- supabase/setup-cli + 'supabase start' in packages/database (fresh stack per job, so db reset is safe); write apps/web/.env pointing at it
- install Chromium with deps via e2e-web
- start the AI stub; run 'pnpm test:e2e' with --reporter list,junit plus @e2e-dev/github for one PR comment per run (needs pull-requests: write + GITHUB_TOKEN; fork PRs get no comment)
- upload .e2e/report.json, junit.xml and .e2e/results on !cancelled()
- secret: the agent's model key only (skip agent steps if unset). No real OpenAI key for the app
- path filter to apps/web/**, apps/e2e/**, packages/database/**

Decide the replay cache policy: CI is read-only by default and starts empty unless .e2e/cache is committed. Committing it cuts model calls and flake, but entries must be reviewed like test data. Record the decision in apps/e2e/README.

Start non-blocking (continue-on-error, as mutation-testing.yml does) until it has run green for a while.
acceptance_criteria:
- A PR touching apps/web runs the suite and posts/updates one results comment
- Reports and failure evidence (screenshots, traces) are downloadable from the run
- Runtime is recorded in the README; target under ~10 minutes
- Cache policy decision written down

title: e2e: upload viva audio, see the transcript, and keep it after navigating away
description:
On a Ready to Record submission, upload a short committed fixture audio file through 'Upload viva audio' (#submissionVivaUpload). Assert the docked player and the stubbed transcript appear, navigate to /submissions and back, and assert the transcript is still there (regression viva-voce-ai-18b). Also confirm the audio streams from storage (film/byte-range route, related viva-voce-ai-2u8).

Live recording: Chromium can feed a fake mic with --use-fake-device-for-media-stream --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream (+ --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture). Add a recording spec only if the web() engine exposes launch args and the realtime socket is handled by the AI stub ticket; otherwise file a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria:
- Upload spec passes offline and asserts the transcript text from the stub
- Transcript survives leave-and-return and a full reload
- Storage object is removed in cleanup
- Live-recording spec added, or a follow-up issue filed saying what blocked it

title: e2e: browse, search and filter submissions against seed data
description:
Read-only journey on /submissions using the seed (2 Awaiting Questions, 1 Ready to Record, 2 Recorded). Cover: list shows the teacher's submissions from Supabase, search narrows by title, status filter (aria-label 'Filter submissions by status') narrows by stage, opening a row goes to /submissions/<id> without flashing an unrelated page (regression viva-voce-ai-2if, if fixed by then).

Keep to cases the page tests can't show: real data through RLS and SSR, real navigation. Leave sort/edge cases to -SubmissionsPage.test.tsx.
acceptance_criteria:
- Specs assert visible counts/titles by role and text, not test ids
- Pass on a fresh seed with no OpenAI access

title: e2e: isolate and clean up test data in the shared local Supabase
description:
Every run, the user's pnpm dev and verify-viva-voce share one local Supabase. Specs that create submissions, questions or audio must not depend on or corrupt each other's rows, and must never run 'supabase db reset' on a stack someone is using.

Approach to evaluate:
- Read-only specs rely on the seed fixtures (see verify-viva-voce features/README.md: 5 submissions, known ids and statuses)
- Mutating specs create their own rows through the UI, tagged '[e2e <runId>]'
- An afterAll/cleanup hook (or e2e project tool via defineTool, see docs: Project tools) deletes tagged rows and storage objects with the service-role key
- Optionally a defineTool seed for preconditions the UI can't reach cheaply (e.g. a Recorded submission with transcript). Setup through a tool is fine, but the behaviour under test must go through the UI
- In CI the stack is fresh per job, so db reset there is safe
acceptance_criteria:
- Running pnpm test:e2e twice in a row passes both times and leaves no tagged rows or storage objects behind
- Seed counts on /submissions are unchanged after a run
- The cleanup refuses to run against a non-local SUPABASE_URL

title: e2e: sign in once as the seed teacher and cover sign-in, sign-up and log-out
description:
Add a test.setup that signs in through /login and saves session 'teacher' (docs: Signing in). Other specs use { session: 'teacher' }. Declare the account under credentials in e2e.config.ts, reading E2E_USER_TEACHER_USERNAME/PASSWORD and defaulting to the seed teacher (will@viva-voce.org) for local runs only.

Specs, each tied to a regression only the running stack shows:
- Sign in lands on /submissions with the teacher's data (SSR cookie + RLS)
- Sign in waits for hydration: the password never appears in the URL (native GET before hydration, see verify-viva-voce Gotchas)
- Unauthenticated /submissions redirects to /login; after log-out, back-navigation doesn't show data
- Sign-up creates an account and signs it in (tag the email, delete the auth user in cleanup)

Verify session.save only after asserting the signed-in screen.
acceptance_criteria:
- Setup test saves 'teacher'; dependent specs start signed in without re-typing credentials
- The four specs above pass locally and fail when the behaviour is broken (sanity-check by breaking it once)
- No credentials are committed apart from the public seed defaults

title: Pin Node to a version the e2e runner supports, locally and in CI
description: e2e requires Node ^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0. deploy-cloudflare.yml and mutation-testing.yml use node-version 20; dev boxes vary (22.22.0 here, 26 in viva-voce-ai-y5q). Pick one version (24 LTS suggested), add .nvmrc + root engines, and update every workflow's setup-node.
acceptance_criteria:
- .nvmrc and package.json engines name the same Node version, within e2e's range
- All workflows use node-version-file: .nvmrc
- pnpm test and pnpm typecheck pass on that version (fix or file what breaks; see viva-voce-ai-y5q for the localStorage/byteRange failures on newer Node)

title: Scaffold apps/e2e workspace package with tester.army e2e and a login smoke test
description:
Create apps/e2e as its own pnpm workspace package so its ai@^7 / @ai-sdk/openai@^4 peers don't collide with apps/web. Run 'pnpm dlx e2e@latest init --yes' there, pin exact versions of e2e and @e2e-dev/web (0.x, breaking changes likely).

e2e.config.ts:
- target: web() with app.command starting 'pnpm --filter web dev --port {port} --strictPort'. The dev server listens on localhost/::1 only (127.0.0.1 doesn't connect, per verify-viva-voce), so use http://localhost:<port>, or make vite bind 127.0.0.1 for e2e and use port 0.
- app.readyUrl /login; startupTimeout >60s (first request compiles the app).
- agents.default model from env (E2E_MODEL / provider key). Keep the agent's key separate from the app's OPENAI_API_KEY.
- .e2e/ results and report gitignored; cache policy decided in the CI ticket.

The runner only starts app.command, so local Supabase must already be up (pnpm db:start). Fail fast with a clear message if SUPABASE_URL isn't http://127.0.0.1:54321, same guard as verify.sh.

Add 'pnpm test:e2e' at the root. Keep e2e out of 'pnpm test' / turbo test so the unit loop stays fast.

Docs: add an 'End-to-end' section to apps/web/TESTING.md (when a behaviour earns an e2e test vs a page test) and a Build & Test line in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. Consider 'npx skills add tester-army/e2e' so agents get the e2e skill.
acceptance_criteria:
- pnpm test:e2e with local Supabase running starts the dev server, opens /login, asserts the sign-in form by role/label, and stops the server it started
- Running it with Supabase down or pointed at a remote project fails with an explanatory message
- pnpm test, pnpm typecheck and pnpm build are unaffected
- TESTING.md says where e2e sits in the strategy

title: Browser e2e suite for teacher journeys (tester.army e2e)
description:
Add a small end-to-end suite that drives the real app (TanStack Start dev server + local Supabase) in Chromium, using the open-source tester.army e2e runner (https://tester.army/e2e, docs https://e2e.tester.army/docs/llms.txt, package 'e2e' 0.21.x, Apache-2.0).

Why: Vitest page tests fake the network and the Start server runtime, so nothing today proves the pieces work together: SSR auth cookies, server functions, Supabase RLS and storage, the login hydration race, route transitions. The verify-viva-voce skill drives the app by hand for agents, but it is not a repeatable regression suite.

Scope: a handful of critical teacher journeys, not a second copy of the page tests. TESTING.md still applies: each e2e test names the regression only a running stack can catch, queries by role/label/text, asserts outcomes (screen + persisted rows).

Constraints found while scoping:
- e2e needs Node ^22.22.3 || >=24.8.0. CI pins Node 20, local is 22.22.0.
- e2e peers on ai@^7 / @ai-sdk/openai@^4. apps/web is on ai@^4 / @ai-sdk/openai@^1, so the suite lives in its own workspace package.
- The app calls OpenAI server-side (generation, transcription, realtime token, assessment summary). Browser-level mocks can't intercept those, so e2e needs a stubbed AI boundary.
- One shared local Supabase stack per machine (see verify-viva-voce SKILL.md: Isolation).

Prefer deterministic screen/expect steps. Use agent.act/agent.assert only where a goal is clearer than locators; agent steps cost model calls.

title: Spike: run Vitest through the TanStack Start plugin so server functions hit MSW

Then count generation requests at the boundary, reach 'reload mid-run' by unmount/remount, and drop the TESTING.md known exception. See apps/web/TESTING.md. Move installFakeRecorder + recordingHandlers from -submissions.$submissionId.test.tsx into src/test/ and reuse: storage 500 -> 'recording chunks failed', 200 -> Retry clears it and chunk row POSTed; getUserMedia rejects then resolves; pause -> 'Resume recording'. See apps/web/TESTING.md. Found in the behaviour-first test audit (viva-voce-ai-sai).

title: Auth tests: real supabase-js against MSW instead of mocking utils/supabase-server
description: Login.test.tsx, -signup.test.tsx, -protected-routes.test.tsx vi.mock our own ../utils/supabase-server. Stub only @tanstack/react-start/server (getCookies -> seeded sb-example-project-auth-token cookie or {}, setCookie noop) and let supabase-js hit MSW: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password, POST /auth/v1/signup, GET /auth/v1/user (authenticatedUserHandler in test/handlers.ts is unused). Assert request bodies. Move the copy-pasted createServerFn stubs (two different shapes) into one shared helper. Add the missing 'Sign Up Instead' branch test (Login.tsx). See apps/web/TESTING.md. Found in the behaviour-first test audit (viva-voce-ai-sai).

title: Add verify-viva-voce skill for driving the real app

title: Stream viva question generation so categories appear as they land
description:
generateSubmissionViva.ts:170 uses generateObject, so nothing can render until the entire 12-question payload is complete. Switching to streamObject lets each category render as it arrives, which is what makes the result-shaped skeleton pay off.

Note the interaction with the superRefine 'exactly 3 recommended per category' constraint — it can only be validated on the complete object, so partial rendering needs to tolerate a late validation failure.
acceptance_criteria: Question categories render progressively as they stream; final validation still enforced; a late validation failure is handled without wiping already-rendered content unexpectedly.

title: Replace static generation shell with staged progress and result-shaped skeleton
description:
SubmissionGenerationShell (submissions.$submissionId.tsx:444) is a static paper panel: a heading and two paragraphs, nothing that moves, and 'This usually takes a few seconds' which understates a 12-question generateObject call.

Reference: Klaviyo's staged checklist (https://mobbin.com/screens/0eff39e1-7398-4098-a38a-55eb4f9d0bb4) — completed steps checked, active step spinning, later steps quiet, plus 'Stay on this page'. Charma (https://mobbin.com/screens/fb4d3c1f-4846-4db9-b5d6-1212b808331d) names an honest upper bound. Chronicle (https://mobbin.com/screens/fbeab89c-f418-442b-9fa2-ba67efa47c56) and GoFundMe (https://mobbin.com/screens/f764e9fc-e5cf-4e0f-89ea-bd778d2fa88a) shape the skeleton like the result.

Work:
- staged list: Submission saved / Reading the submission / Drafting questions / Writing teacher notes
- skeleton in the real output shape: 3 real category headings, 4 skeleton question cards each
- replace 'a few seconds' with a measured upper bound
- re-skin to DESIGN.md: navy not green, 3px radius, hairline rules, technical shadow only, no whimsical microcopy
acceptance_criteria: Waiting state shows movement and structure; category headings are real; time estimate matches measured p90; passes DESIGN.md tone and token rules.

title: Give students a human-readable reference
description: public.students has only id and created_at, so the submissions list can only identify a student by UUID. The table now shows the first UUID segment ('Student 10420000') with the full value on hover, which is a stopgap - prefixes can collide and it means nothing to a teacher. Add a name or student reference number to the students table and surface that instead.

title: Decide the fate of the question-set and readiness components
description: The detail page redesign dropped the ready-for-viva ceremony. Now orphaned (only their own tests use them): -QuestionSetPanel.tsx, -VivaSessionReadinessPanel.tsx, the isInSet/onToggleInSet branch of -QuestionCard.tsx, useEquipmentCheck, and the readiness half of features/submissions/vivaSession.ts. Either delete them or fold the parts worth keeping (recording consent, in particular) into the Record flow.
notes: 2026-10-10 (branch test/behaviour-first-strategy, viva-voce-ai-sai): Sam chose delete. Removed -QuestionSetPanel, -VivaSessionReadinessPanel, their tests, evaluateReadiness/startVivaSession and the reorder helpers in vivaQuestionSet.ts. title: Redesign submission detail page around a Record CTA
description: The submissions/:id page is cluttered: tabs, a sticky sidebar with three stage panels, and the submission text hidden behind a tab. Rework it into a simple linear page: Record panel (inert placeholder for now) -> full submission text -> viva questions -> question set / readiness / evidence. Remove the tabs and the sticky rail.

title: Redesign submissions list page
description: The submissions index is clunky: decorative KPI tiles that DESIGN.md bans, no search/filter/sort, invalid tr role=link semantics, no row dividers or panel chrome, 10px chips below the 12px label floor, bare text loading/error states, and a mobile layout with no row separation. Rebuild the page around a working toolbar (search + status filter carrying the counts), a properly chromed sortable table, stacked mobile cards, skeleton loading, and an error state with retry.

title: Add submission links and generation status to the submissions list
description:
Update the submissions list so teachers can find and revisit generated viva analyses easily.

Why:
Once submissions gain their own detail pages and generation status, the list page needs to expose those entry points and states.

Work:
- link each submission row or card to its detail page
- expose generation status in the list UI so teachers can see whether analysis is pending, ready, or failed
- keep the list behavior aligned with the detail-page data model

Acceptance criteria:
- each submission in the list links to its detail page
- the list makes generation state visible at a glance
- the list remains usable while some submissions are still generating or have generation failures

description:
public/landing-hero-workspace.png is 1.7MB at 1448x1086, served as a raw PNG with no responsive sources. The three landing-step-*.png files (1.5-1.8MB each, ~5.1MB total) are now unused after the how-it-works section moved to a numbered type treatment.

Delete the unused step images and convert the hero to WebP/AVIF with a srcset.

title: Landing hero promises a three-pane workspace the app doesn't ship
description:
public/landing-hero-workspace.png shows a three-column workspace (Submission | Viva questions | Teacher notes). The shipped submission page is a single-column stack of panels.

Confirmed as a known roadmap gap rather than an image to swap out. Same underlying gap as the conduct-mode layout work: the app has no two-pane workspace anywhere.

Either build the layout or reshoot the hero before the pilot widens.
acceptance_criteria: Either the submission page offers a multi-pane layout, or the hero reflects what ships.

title: font-serif in the readiness panel bypasses the Newsreader token
description:
-VivaSessionReadinessPanel.tsx:217 uses 'font-serif' on a <dd>. No --font-serif token exists in app.css (only --font-display: 'Newsreader', serif), so this renders in the browser's default serif stack rather than the design system's display face.

The same bug in submissions.$submissionId.tsx was fixed by the new readingClassName, but this instance is a different typographic context — body-size serif in a definition list, which is not a documented step either. Decide whether it should be the documented reading step, a body step, or a new one, rather than reaching for font-serif again.
acceptance_criteria: No font-serif remains in the codebase; the readiness panel renders in a documented step.

title: Document a reading type step and use it for submission text
description:
submissions.$submissionId.tsx:1218 sets the student's submission text with a literal 'font-serif text-[19px] leading-[1.75]' — off the DESIGN.md type ramp, and a near-miss of the lede step (18px/1.7). DESIGN.md has no step for continuous long-form reading; lede is scoped to standfirst copy.

Separately, 'font-serif' resolves to Tailwind's default serif stack rather than Newsreader, because no --font-serif token exists — only --font-display. So the reading surface is not using the design system's display face.

Add a documented 'reading' step (Newsreader, 19px, 1.75) to DESIGN.md and a matching readingClassName in lib/class-names.ts, then use it at the call site.
acceptance_criteria: DESIGN.md documents the reading step; readingClassName exists and is used for submission text; the text renders in Newsreader; the design hook no longer flags the line.
close_reason: Documented the reading step, added readingClassName, applied it to submission text.

title: Schema miscount throws away the whole generation wait
description:
The schema demands exactly 4 questions and exactly 3 recommended per category (generateSubmissionViva.ts, superRefine). JSON Schema cannot express the count, so the model has to get it right — and a miscount fails the entire response with a ZodError after the teacher has already waited the full generation time. They get a Try again button and nothing else.

Consider a server-side retry on validation failure, or accepting the questions and relaxing the recommended-count constraint to a post-processing step.
acceptance_criteria: A model miscount does not cost the teacher the full wait with zero output.

title: New submission button label does not match what it does
description:
submissions.new.tsx:118 labels the submit button 'Generate viva questions' but its loading copy reads 'Saving the submission.' — the button only performs the insert. The mismatch sets the wrong expectation at the first click of the slowest flow in the app.

Align the label and the in-flight copy with what actually happens at each stage.
acceptance_criteria: Button label and loading copy describe the same action; copy stays in the DESIGN.md register (no whimsy).
close_reason: Loading copy now names both the save and the generation start.

title: Reconsider 'Ready for Viva' status vocabulary on the submissions list
description: The submissions list still buckets rows as Pending Questions / Ready for Viva / Recorded, and 'ready for viva' was the draft-to-ready state that the detail page no longer has. Decide what status means now that the flow is submission -> questions -> recording.
close_reason: Status vocabulary reworked with the list redesign: 'Pending Questions' -> 'Awaiting Questions', 'Ready for Viva' -> 'Ready to Record'. Labels now match the record-first detail page.

title: Authed page content has no max measure on wide screens
description: AuthenticatedAppShell renders <main className='min-w-0 px-6 pb-16 pt-8'> with no max-width, while lib/class-names.ts defines pageFrameClassName with max-w-[1328px] that nothing applies. On a wide monitor every authed page — the submissions table especially — stretches edge to edge, which breaks the reading measure DESIGN.md asks for. Decide whether PageFrame or the app shell owns the measure and apply it in one place.

value: Tailwind v4 token trap in apps/web/src/styles/app.css: the '@theme inline' block must not redefine a token that ':root' maps back to it. '--color-primary: var(--primary)' plus '--primary: var(--color-primary)' is a cycle, so the variable resolves to nothing and every bg-primary/text-primary in the app renders transparent. It silently killed the submissions status chips and the active sidebar item. Check for cycles between the '@theme inline' block and ':root' when adding tokens.
